note: Close to core on four criteria and fails the fifth for an unusual reason. A 32-year-old Swiss corporate professional who owns suits, funds a personal trainer and a nutritionist, and has paid for blood panel analysis is comfortably inside 'successful' and 'makes good money' — the price shock ('definitely wasn't expecting the cost') is surprise rather than an affordability statement, and he never said he could not pay. He is emphatically not the excluded profile: ex-army, currently training with a coach, averaging 13,000 to 16,000 steps a day. And the goal is good to great — 87kg down to 75-78kg with muscle, framed as refinement rather than rescue. Where he fails is 'neglected health', and he fails it by having the opposite problem: health is one of the more actively managed parts of his life, with a trainer, a nutritionist, blood work and a cortisol protocol already in place. That is the same failure mode as Brian Begin and Stephanie Lee in this batch — the ICP assumes health is the underinvested corner, and a meaningful share of the people who reach a closer call have already invested in it heavily.
